title: Torus equivariance of any smooth-functorial normalized tower rule
statement:
Let $H$ assign to every reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme $X$, including finite disjoint unions [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], a finite tower $X_n\to\cdots\to X_0=X$ of normalized blowups [def-trf-normalized-blowup], remembering coherent ideal centers $J_i\subset\mathcal O_{X_i}$ with nonempty nowhere dense zero schemes. Suppose that for every smooth $h:Y\to X$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] there is a canonical comparison $H(Y)\simeq(h^*H(X))^c$ of recursively pulled-back towers, retaining extended ideals in order and deleting exactly unit-ideal stages whose arrows are isomorphisms. Suppose these comparisons respect identities and composition, and no stage is deleted for a surjective $h$.

Let $r\geq0$, let $T=\mathbf G_{m,\mathbf Q}^r=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$ with coordinatewise multiplication, inverse and identity $1$, and let $a_0:T\times_{\mathbf Q}X\to X$ be an action: $a_0(1,x)=x$ and $a_0(t,a_0(u,x))=a_0(tu,x)$ as scheme morphisms. Then $T\times_{\mathbf Q}X$ is reduced of finite type, the projection $p_0$ and action $a_0$ are smooth and surjective, and the two comparisons give a canonical identification
$$p_0^*H(X)\simeq H(T\times_{\mathbf Q}X)\simeq a_0^*H(X)$$
of uncontracted towers with their ordered ideal centers.

There is a unique family of actions $a_i:T\times_{\mathbf Q}X_i\to X_i$ extending $a_0$ such that every transition $b_i:X_{i+1}\to X_i$ is equivariant. If $p_i$ is projection, these actions satisfy
$$a_i^*J_i=p_i^*J_i,\qquad b_i\circ a_{i+1}=a_i\circ(1_T\times b_i).$$
The action $a_{i+1}$ is the projection to $X_{i+1}$ after the canonical comparison
$$T\times_{\mathbf Q}X_{i+1}\simeq X_{i+1}\times_{X_i,a_i}(T\times_{\mathbf Q}X_i)$$
of the normalized blowups of the equal ideals $p_i^*J_i=a_i^*J_i$; it satisfies the unit and associativity identities as morphisms of schemes. In particular every center ideal, rather than only its underlying closed set, is $T$-invariant. No regularity hypothesis on the last level and no toric hypothesis on $X$ is required.

source.place: Expose VIII, 2.1.11, Proposition 2.2.4(i), Lemma 2.2.9 and Corollary 2.3.17 with its proof, printed pp.88,90--91,94--95; stated for any tower rule with the indicated smooth comparisons, specialized to split tori. The normalized lifting induction is the retained proof step 6. No Stacks tag states this functorial-tower assertion.

proof.text: Use $L=\mathbf Z^r$ with its standard basis. The coordinate isomorphism of [lem-trf-lattice-torus-coordinates-action] identifies $\mathbf Q[L]$ and its group operations with the specified $T$, and gives finite type of $Y=T\times_{\mathbf Q}X$. By [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection], $Y$ is reduced and $p_0$ is smooth and surjective. The morphism $F_0(t,x)=(t,a_0(t,x))$ is an automorphism over $T$: its inverse is $(t,x)\mapsto(t,a_0(t^{-1},x))$, by the two assumed action identities. Thus $a_0=p_0\circ F_0$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition] (an isomorphism is smooth directly from [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]) and surjective. The same projection facts apply to every reduced finite-type level and to $T^2$, using $L=\mathbf Z^{2r}$.

source.place: VIII 2.3.17, proof, p.95: smoothness of projection and action; lattice-coordinate specialization of 3.2.2, p.103.

proof.text: The hypotheses on $H$ applied to the two smooth surjections give uncontracted, center-preserving tower isomorphisms $p_0^*H(X)\simeq H(Y)\simeq a_0^*H(X)$. Put $q_i:X_i\to X$ for the structural map, $P_i=T\times X_i$, and $A_i=Y\times_{X,a_0}X_i$. Repeated application of [lem-trf-normalized-blowup-calculus] identifies these recursive pullbacks with these ordinary fibre products: at each step its smooth comparison also makes the next level map smooth. It also makes every $X_i$ reduced of finite type. Write $E_i:P_i\xrightarrow{\sim}A_i$ for the comparison, over $Y$; it respects transitions and ordered extended ideals. Define $a_i=\operatorname{pr}_{X_i}\circ E_i$. At level zero this is $a_0$, and transition compatibility gives $b_i\circ a_{i+1}=a_i\circ(1_T\times b_i)$.

source.place: VIII 2.2.9, p.91, and 2.3.17, proof, p.95: compare the two entire towers before lifting centers.

proof.text: Here is the rigidity argument used below. Any automorphism of $H(X)$ inducing the identity on $X_0$ is the identity at every level: start at level zero; if its component on $X_i$ is the identity, its component on $X_{i+1}$ is an $X_i$-automorphism of the normalized blowup, hence is the identity by [lem-trf-normalized-blowup-calculus]. The identical induction works for the uncontracted pullback along any smooth map from a reduced finite-type scheme, since that lemma identifies each pulled arrow with the normalized blowup of the extended nowhere dense ideal. Consequently any two tower isomorphisms having the same base map have equal components: compose one with the inverse of the other and apply this induction.

source.place: VIII 2.2.3--2.2.4(i), p.90; iterative uniqueness used in 2.3.17, p.95.

proof.text: There is an isomorphism $K_i:A_i\xrightarrow{\sim}T\times X_i$ given by $((t,x),z)\mapsto(t,z)$; its inverse sends $(t,z)$ to $((t,a_0(t^{-1},q_i(z))),z)$. The fibre-product equation holds by the action identities on $X$. Hence $F_i=K_iE_i$, whose formula is $(t,z)\mapsto(t,a_i(t,z))$, is an isomorphism over $T$, compatible with every transition. Its base change along $1:\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q\to T$ is an automorphism of the original tower over $X$, since $F_0(1,x)=(1,x)$. The rigidity induction of Step 3, using the automorphism clause of [lem-trf-normalized-blowup-calculus], gives $a_i(1,z)=z$ as a scheme morphism. No smoothness of the unit section is used.

source.place: VIII 2.1.11, p.88: unit identity; normalized uniqueness from 2.2.4(i), p.90.

proof.text:
On $T\times T\times X_i$ consider the tower isomorphisms over $T^2$
$$U_i(t,u,z)=(t,u,a_i(t,a_i(u,z))),\qquad V_i(t,u,z)=(t,u,a_i(tu,z)).$$
The first is the composite of the two base changes of $F_i$ under the projections to $t$ and $u$; the second is its base change under multiplication $T^2\to T$. They are isomorphisms even without knowing the lifted associativity law. On level zero $U_0=V_0$ by the given associativity of $a_0$. Therefore $(V_i^{-1}U_i)_i$ is a tower automorphism over the identity of $T^2\times X$. Its underlying tower is the pullback along $T^2\times X\to X$, a smooth projection by [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection]. Step 3 and [lem-trf-normalized-blowup-calculus] force it to be the identity. Thus $U_i=V_i$, proving $a_i(t,a_i(u,z))=a_i(tu,z)$ as morphisms. All the displayed formulas denote product and fibre-product morphisms, rather than just maps on field-valued points.

source.place: VIII 2.1.11, p.88: associativity via the action nerve; 2.2.4(i) and 2.2.9, pp.90--91: normalized version.

proof.text:
Since $E_i$ preserves the ordered ideals, pulling the ideal from $X_i$ through its $A_i$ projection gives exactly the ideal pulled through the $P_i$ projection. Thus $a_i^*J_i=p_i^*J_i$ as extended ideal sheaves, not merely equality of their zero sets. The now-established action has graph isomorphism $F_i$, so $a_i=p_i\circ F_i$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition] and [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; $p_i$ is smooth by [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection]. Apply [lem-trf-normalized-blowup-calculus] to these two maps at the single arrow $b_i$. Both resulting pullbacks are the normalized blowup of the equal ideal on $T\times X_i$. Their canonical identification is therefore
$$T\times X_{i+1}\simeq X_{i+1}\times_{X_i,a_i}(T\times X_i).$$
The comparison induced by $a_{i+1}$ is another such identification: its graph is an isomorphism, and transition equivariance gives its fibre-product equation. Their ratio is an automorphism over $T\times X_i$ of that normalized blowup, hence the identity by the same calculus lemma. Its second projection is consequently the specified $a_{i+1}$.

source.place: VIII 2.3.17, proof, p.95: center invariance and induction; 2.1.11, p.88, and 2.2.4(i), 2.2.9, pp.90--91: canonical normalized lift.

proof.text: For uniqueness let $(\widetilde a_i)$ be any other family of actions with the given $a_0$ and equivariant transitions. Its graph $\widetilde F_i(t,z)=(t,\widetilde a_i(t,z))$ is an isomorphism over $T$, with inverse $(t,z)\mapsto(t,\widetilde a_i(t^{-1},z))$. Thus $(F_i^{-1}\widetilde F_i)_i$ is an automorphism of the projection pullback tower over the identity on $T\times X$. The projection is smooth by [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection], so Step 3, using [lem-trf-normalized-blowup-calculus], gives $F_i=\widetilde F_i$ and $a_i=\widetilde a_i$ for every $i$. This did not assume invariance of the alternative centers. Length zero, empty $X$, rank zero and disconnected $X$ are allowed throughout; for rank zero the unit identity gives the identity action. No regular endpoint or toric structure was used.

source.place: VIII 2.2.4(i), p.90, and 2.3.17, pp.94--95: unique normalized lifting.
